key_insight: A symmetric graded-mesh Galerkin FEM with an auxiliary variable reformulates the delayed time-fractional diffusion-wave problem into a stable coupled system with provable error control.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical and theoretically grounded solver for delayed fractional diffusion-wave models used in materials, transport, and viscoelastic simulation.
method: Introduce an auxiliary variable and symmetric fractional-order reduction to obtain an equivalent coupled system.
Discretise time with the L1 scheme on a symmetric graded mesh and space with standard finite elements.
Prove stability via a discrete fractional Grönwall inequality and derive local truncation/error estimates using a new barrier-function comparison principle.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports rigorous regularity analysis, stability and convergence proofs, and numerical experiments that confirm the theoretical results.
watch_item: The method relies on symmetric graded time meshes and careful barrier-function construction, so implementation may be sensitive to mesh design and parameter choices.
paper_title: Galerkin finite element method for time fractional diffusion-wave equations with constant time delay
